name: Obligations
rows: MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(b) entirely; only (b)(1) detailed criteria exempt. Baseline risk assessment under 314.4(b) still required.
No written risk assessment exists; only generic onboarding training completed
Commission a written risk assessment covering CIA of customer information, risk categorization criteria, and mitigation approach; engage Qualified Individual to approve
Qualified Individual (to be designated) + Dana Lee (Compliance)
Signed written risk assessment document; Qualified Individual sign-off
MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(a). The 'Qualified Individual' requirement is distinct from the old 'designate an employee' standard.
No QI designated; old 2021 rule only required 'designate an employee to coordinate'
Designate a Qualified Individual (employee, affiliate, or service provider); if using service provider/affiliate, retain responsibility, designate senior overseer, and require equivalent ISP
Written designation memo; senior oversight assignment; service provider contract if applicable
MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(c)(5). MFA required for any individual accessing any information system unless QI approves equivalent/more secure controls in writing.
Deploy MFA for all information system access; obtain written QI approval only if equivalent/more secure alternative used
MFA deployment logs; QI written approval if alternative used
No continuous monitoring / penetration testing / vulnerability assessments

EXEMPT — §314.6 expressly exempts §314.4(d)(2) for institutions maintaining <5000 consumers. NOTE: §314.4(d)(1) (general testing/monitoring) is NOT exempt; only (d)(2) specific continuous monitoring/pen test/vuln assessment cadence is exempt.
No pen testing, no vuln assessments, no continuous monitoring in place

VOLUNTARY best practice: adopt annual pen test + semi-annual vuln assessment anyway given active incident. MANDATORY under 314.4(d)(1): implement some form of regular testing/monitoring of key controls
Testing schedule; first test report; 314.4(d)(1) key-controls monitoring procedure
EXEMPT — §314.6 expressly exempts §314.4(h) for <5000 consumers. NOTE: this is a size-based exception, NOT a blanket exemption from incident response.
No written IRP; ad-hoc response underway for current event
VOLUNTARY best practice: draft written IRP covering 314.4(h)(1)-(7) elements given active incident. MANDATORY: continue responding to current event under 314.4(j) notification obligation
Dana Lee + Qualified Individual + external counsel
Draft IRP document; incident response logs for current event
VOLUNTARY best practice: establish annual reporting cadence; for current event, brief senior officer immediately given 314.4(i) exemption does not eliminate accountability
Voluntary: next board cycle; current event: 7 days
Board minutes or senior officer briefing memo
EXEMPT — §314.6 exempts §314.4(b)(1) detailed written criteria for <5000 consumers. NOTE: baseline risk assessment under 314.4(b) still required; only the detailed sub-criteria are exempt.
16 CFR 314.4(b)(1) exempt per 314.6; 314.4(b) baseline mandatory; frozen XML
Conduct baseline risk assessment per 314.4(b); detailed (b)(1) criteria are voluntary best practice for this size
Cloud services contract lacks security obligations
MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(f). Service provider oversight fully applies.
Cloud contract has no security obligations clause
Renegotiate cloud contract to require safeguards; periodically assess provider risk; select/retain only capable providers
Amended contract with security clause; provider assessment record
MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(e). Training must be updated to reflect risks identified.
Generic onboarding completed; no ongoing updates
Implement periodic security awareness updates tied to risk assessment findings; verify key personnel maintain current threat knowledge
Training materials; attendance logs; refresher schedule
No encryption of customer information at rest/in transit
MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(c)(3). Encryption required unless QI approves alternative compensating controls in writing.
Current event involved encrypted export BUT key was also obtained — encryption alone insufficient if key management fails
Review encryption posture; implement key management controls separate from encrypted storage; QI to review compensating controls if encryption infeasible
Encryption inventory; key management procedure; QI approval if alternative used
Implement secure disposal procedure (≤2 years after last use); periodic data retention review
Disposal procedure; retention policy; disposal logs
No access controls / data inventory / change management / user activity monitoring
Current event shows attacker accessed and downloaded export file — indicates weak access controls
Implement/ review access controls, data inventory, secure dev practices, change management, user activity monitoring
Access control policy; data inventory; change management log; user activity monitoring config
MANDATORY — §314.6 does NOT exempt 314.4(j). 550 consumers ≥ 500 threshold triggers notification.
Submit FTC notification electronically by 2025-04-02 (30 days from discovery); draft notice now; preserve law enforcement contact info
FTC electronic submission confirmation; copy of notice
